title: How early should you arrive at Cardiff Airport?
author: Matt
cover_image_alt: A plane parked at an airport gate, seen through a terminal window covered in rain
intro: Cardiff is a small, one-terminal airport, so two hours before a holiday flight is usually plenty. Here's how much time to allow for your airline, your bags and the busy mornings, and how to get there.
seo_description: About 2 hours before most flights from Cardiff, 2½ if you're checking bags at a busy time and 3 for long-haul. Times by airline, security and transport.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Short-haul, hand luggage:** about 1½ to 2 hours
- **Short-haul, checked bags:** about 2 hours
- **Long-haul with TUI:** about 3 hours
- **Busy mornings and holidays:** add 30 mins

These are our suggestions, not airport rules. The times that really matter are your airline's check-in and bag drop deadlines, which are in your booking. Advice and rules change, so check with the airport or your airline before you fly. We checked the details below in November 2026.

sections.heading: Why Cardiff is usually quick
sections.text:
Cardiff is one of the UK's smaller airports. It handled just under a million passengers in 2025, according to Welsh Government figures, compared with around ten times that at Bristol. There's one terminal, and the walk from the door to security to the gates is short.

The catch is that its flights come in waves. Most of the holiday flights, especially TUI's, leave in the early morning, so check-in and security can be busy for an hour or two and then go quiet. If your flight is in that first wave, or it's a Saturday in the school holidays, allow the extra half an hour.

sections.heading: How early for your airline
sections.text:
| Airline | Flies to | Our suggestion | Check-in or bag drop closes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TUI | Package holidays and flights to the sun | 2 hours (3 for long-haul) | Usually about an hour before; check your booking |
| Ryanair | Spain, Portugal, the Canaries, Dublin | 2 hours with bags | Bag drop closes 40 mins before |
| KLM | Amsterdam, with onward connections | 2 hours, more if connecting long-haul | Check your booking |
| Vueling | Spain, in summer | 2 hours | Check your booking |

TUI flights are often full charters with lots of families checking bags at once, which is why the bag drop queue is usually the slowest part. Many TUI customers can check in online, but you'll still need to queue to drop a hold bag.

Tip: if you're flying with Ryanair with hand luggage only, check in online and download your boarding pass before you leave home. You can then go straight to security, and 1½ hours is usually enough outside the busy waves.

sections.heading: Security and liquids
sections.text:
Cardiff has new CT security scanners, so you can usually leave laptops and liquids in your bag. But the **100ml limit still applies** to each liquid container in your hand luggage. Unlike Birmingham or Heathrow, Cardiff hasn't raised the limit to 2 litres.

- **Liquids:** containers of 100ml or less, which can stay in your bag.
- **Electronics:** can usually stay in your bag too.
- **Larger liquids:** put them in your hold bag, or buy them after security.

Watch out: the rules differ between UK airports, and the airport you fly home from may have different scanners. Pack liquids for the stricter rule, so you don't have to throw anything away on the way back.

sections.heading: Getting to Cardiff Airport
sections.text:
The airport is at Rhoose in the Vale of Glamorgan, about 12 miles south-west of Cardiff city centre, so allow for the journey as well as the time at the airport.

- **By train:** take the Vale of Glamorgan line from Cardiff Central to Rhoose Cardiff International Airport station, then a short shuttle bus to the terminal. Trains are usually hourly, and less often on Sundays, so check the times for an early flight.
- **By bus:** bus links to the city centre have changed several times in recent years, so check the airport's website for the current service.
- **By car:** there are short and long stay car parks, and booking ahead is usually cheaper. There's a charge to drop off by the terminal, so check the current price, or use the car park options shown on the airport's website.
- **By taxi:** about half an hour from central Cardiff, depending on traffic.

For a first-wave flight, the first trains often won't get you there in time, so most people drive, take a taxi or stay nearby the night before.

sections.heading: At the gate
sections.text: Once you're through security, there's one departure lounge with shops, a café and a bar, and the gates are a short walk away. Boarding usually starts about 30 to 40 minutes before departure, and the gate closes before that, so don't wait for a final call. If you're connecting with KLM through Amsterdam, your bags are normally checked through to your final destination. Our guide to [where you can fly direct from Cardiff](/blog/where-can-you-fly-direct-from-cardiff-airport) lists the routes, and [Bristol](/blog/how-early-should-you-arrive-at-bristol-airport), about an hour away, is the bigger alternative.

sections.heading: Where could you go from Cardiff?
sections.text:
Most of Cardiff's flights are to the sun, so a week away is easy to plan:

- **Winter sun:** [Lanzarote](/destinations/lanzarote), [Fuerteventura](/destinations/fuerteventura) or [Gran Canaria](/destinations/gran-canaria)
- **Summer:** [Mallorca](/destinations/mallorca), the [Algarve](/destinations/algarve) or [Tenerife](/destinations/tenerife)
- **A weekend away:** [Amsterdam](/destinations/amsterdam) with KLM

If you can't agree on one, read our guide to [deciding where to go on holiday](/how-to-decide-where-to-go-on-holiday), or put your shortlist into a draw on somewhere.party.

faqs.question: How early should I get to Cardiff Airport?
faqs.answer: About 2 hours before a short-haul flight if you're checking a bag, and about 3 hours for long-haul. With hand luggage only and an online boarding pass, 1½ hours is usually enough outside busy times.

faqs.question: Is Cardiff Airport security quick?
faqs.answer: Usually, because it's a small, one-terminal airport. It can be busy for an hour or two in the early morning, when most holiday flights leave.

faqs.question: What is the liquids limit at Cardiff Airport?
faqs.answer: 100ml per container in hand luggage. Cardiff has new scanners, so liquids can usually stay in your bag, but it hasn't moved to the 2-litre limit.

faqs.question: Is there a train to Cardiff Airport?
faqs.answer: Yes, to Rhoose Cardiff International Airport station on the Vale of Glamorgan line, then a short shuttle bus to the terminal. Check the timetable for early flights.
